newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
PREMIER DISOWNS LETTER TO INVESTIGATING AGENCY

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda told the United Front (UF) Steering Committee meeting that he did not support a letter from his Department of Personnel that sought to clip the wings of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). He described as absolutely unauthorised the letter to the CBI regarding curtailing its powers to investigate charges against current and former cabinet ministers. The UF Steering Committee also pulled up the left parties for rushing to the press instead of confining criticism of the government within the Front.
The Times Of India
ELECTION COMMISSION CALLS FOR ELECTORAL REFORMS

The Election Commission (EC) reaffirmed that a loophole in the electoral law which makes a mockery of the ceiling on election expenditure should be plugged. At its meeting with the chief electoral officers, the EC regretted the government's delay in responding to the commission's suggestion that the expenditure ceiling of candidates for both parliamentary and assembly elections be raised from 450,000 rupees to 1.5 million rupees and 150,000 rupees to about 600,000 rupees, respectively. Election Commissioner G.V. Krishnamurty said rule making authority under the Representation of Peoples' Act should be with the commission instead of the government.
The Economic Times
PRIVATE ROAD DEVELOPERS ASSURED TRAFFIC FLOW

The government announced new guidelines for facilitating private investment in the road sector. The government decided to offer an assured traffic flow to the private developers in the road sector, failing which it would compensate the private companies for the losses suffered. Also, the land acquired for road development by private parties would have legal immunity against possible litigation by displaced dwellers. The government also announced certain fiscal incentives to companies intending to invest in infrastructure facilities in the highway sector.
GREEN SIGNAL FOR STOCK-LENDING

The Finance Ministry cleared the stock lending scheme which would stipulate a net worth of 500 million rupees for designated intermediaries. It also decided that capital gains tax would not be applicable to the stock lending scheme. According to the scheme suggested by the Securities and Exchange Board of India, a new system of intermediaries would be introduced. This system would allow intermediaries to lend shares in the market. These shares could be owned by the intermediaries themselves or other sources. The designated intermediaries would include financial institutions, banks, custodians, clearing houses with a net worth of 500 million rupees to ensure safety of the transaction.
TELECOMMUNICATION WATCHDOG TO BE MORE POWERFUL

The cabinet approved the setting up of the Telecommunication Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) with more powers and freedom than the earlier TRAI bill. Now the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) would also be under the purview of the TRAI. In the earlier TRAI bill DoT was not under its jurisdiction. This was a long pending demand of the private telecommunication services operators. In the original draft, prior permission of government was required for making any changes in the rules and regulations. The new regulator would not have to seek government's permission every time before making an amendment in the rules.
Financial Express
EXCHANGE RISK LOSS FOR APEX BANK AT 21 BLN RUPEES

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) would book a loss of over 21 billion rupees to bear the exchange risk on the entire corpus of $2.2 billion India Development Bonds (IDBs). The first tranche of the country's first sovereign bond by proxy was redeemed on Wednesday. RBI paid $231 million towards the redemption of IDBs held by non-resident Indians. RBI sources said the rest of the amount accounted for by transfer of the bonds to the residents was redeemed in rupees. The total corpus of the IDB series-I was $418 million.
GOVERNMENT TO HOLD 40 PCT STAKE IN INFRASTRUCTURE BODY

The cabinet cleared a proposal to set up the 50 billion rupee Infrastructure Development Finance Company (IDFC) as a non-government company with the powers of management vested in an independent board of directors. The IDFC is being set up with the purpose of providing financial and non-financial support for funding infrastructure projects in sectors such as power, telecommunications, roadways, ports, airports, railways, industrial parks, water supply, sanitation, waterways and urban transport system.
SHARE PRICES FLARE UP

Stock prices flared up on local bourses. In a heated trading session on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), the 30-share BSE Sensitive index zoomed 154.47 points to cross the 3,6OO level. The National Stock Exchange's (NSE) 50-share index jumped 52.50 points to close at 1,O41.80 from the overnight close of 989.30. For the first time in the history of the BSE, the volume crossed the 10 billion rupee mark and touched 11.93 billion rupees. Taking into account the NSE volume of 15.25 billion rupees, the total volume on both the exchanges shot up to 27.18 billion rupees.
FIAT TO INVEST 20 BLN RUPEES IN PALIO VENTURE

Fiat Auto of Italy plans to invest 20 billion rupees in a venture near Pune for the manufacture of its Palio range of cars. Fiat would pick up 74 percent stake while the rest would be held by the Vinod Doshi family. Sources said Fiat-controlled World Car would entail the manufacture of the hatchback Palio, 1,700 cc Siena or the sedan and the diesel station wagon in India. The joint venture would have an equity of 9.1 billion rupees. Sources said the joint venture company would have a total capacity of 100,000 units.
AMBANIS JOIN CONFEDERATION OF INDIAN INDUSTRIES

After keeping away from active participation in industry associations for years, Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) of the Ambanis became a member of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII). RIL sources said the move to join CII was based on the Reliance group's decision to play a more active role in industry circles. Sources said even if the Ambanis decided to stay away from the limelight, the group's considerable clout in government and industrial circles was expected to make an impact on CII's stance in key issues.
Business Standard
TELECOM MAJOR'S GDR ISSUE LIKELY TO BE POSTPONED

The proposed global depositary receipts (GDR) issue of Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd is likely to be postponed. The offering was earlier planned to hit international markets in February this year. However, due to delays in the selection of co-lead managers to the issue, the GDR offering might be postponed to March or April, government sources said.
NORTHWEST TO START INDIA FLIGHTS IN JUNE

U.S.-based Northwest Airlines announced that it would launch its Indian operations on June 3, in alliance with KLM Royal Dutch Airlines. Northwest vice-president (Atlantic region) David.C. Wookey said the company was in talks with Indian Airlines to forge an alliance or a code-sharing arrangement. He, however, added that nothing concrete had emerged so far. Wookey said Northwest was also looking for a marketing arrangement with Air-India for destinations like Bangkok, Singapore and Tokyo, and was open to tie-ups with private domestic carriers like Jet Airways.
The Observer
MAJOR CHANGES IN CARRY-FORWARD SYSTEM LIKELY

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is planning major relaxations in the carry-forward system to make it practical and acceptable to market participants. Among the stipulations where the market regulator is planning relaxations, are a cut in margin daily reporting norms and more flexibility in carryforward transactions. The SEBI is also likely to make changes in the limit on carryforward transactions by brokers out of their total transactions in a day and allowing brokers to square up transactions marked as carryforward during a settlement period.
